title: Affine quotient of a free split-torus action is the spectrum of invariants
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $A$ be a finite-type commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$ for a finite integer $r\geq0$ [def-sc-gm-ga] act on $X$ over $S$ by a morphism satisfying the action identities [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume the action is free on all $S$-schemes: for every $S$-scheme $V$, $t\cdot x=x$ with $t\in T(V)$ and $x\in X(V)$ implies $t=1$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $A^T=\{a\in A:\rho(a)=1\otimes a\}$, where $\rho:A\to R[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]\otimes_RA$ is the coaction; equivalently $A^T=A_0$ for the associated $\mathbf Z^r$-grading. Then the fppf sheafification of $V\mapsto X(V)/T(V)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Spec}(A^T)$, with quotient morphism induced by $A^T\hookrightarrow A$ [def-pc-fppf-site] [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. In particular this fppf quotient is affine over $S$; the statement concerns a free action, not a categorical quotient for an arbitrary action.

source.place: Sections 1.2.3 and 1.3.1, printed pp.4–6, arXiv:2201.06424v4: affine free-action quotient for a reductive group (reference there to Alper Proposition 9.7.8), specialized to a split torus; identification of its affine algebra as invariants by the sheaf equalizer. WANTED local copy.

proof.text: Write $M=\mathbf Z^r$. Expand $\rho(a)=\sum_{m\in M}t^m\otimes p_m(a)$. Counit gives $a=\sum_m p_m(a)$; coassociativity, by comparing Laurent coefficients, gives $p_n p_m=0$ for $n\ne m$ and $p_m^2=p_m$. Thus $A_m=\operatorname{im}p_m$ are additive subgroups with $A=\bigoplus_m A_m$. Since $\rho$ is an algebra homomorphism, $A_mA_n\subseteq A_{m+n}$, $1\in A_0$, and the image of $R$ lies in $A_0$. Comparing coefficients again gives $A^T=A_0$. This is the coefficient proof of Tag 0EKK with multi-indices in place of integers; no reducedness or field hypothesis is used.

In $A[M]=A[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, form $I=(a(t^m-1):a\in A_m)$ and $J=(t^m-1:m\in M)$. Clearly $I\subseteq J$. Put $C=A[M]/I$. Its coefficient homomorphism $A\to C$ gives $x\in X(\operatorname{Spec}C)$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; the images of the $t_i$ are units and give $t\in T(\operatorname{Spec}C)$. Each homogeneous $a$ satisfies $x(a)t^m=x(a)$ by the defining relations, hence $t\cdot x=x$ on all of $A$. Freeness on this particular $S$-scheme forces every $t_i=1$ in $C$. The quotient kernel is $I$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], so $t_i-1\in I$ and therefore $J\subseteq I$. We have proved $I=J$ without replacing scheme-theoretic freeness by freeness on geometric points.

source.place: Tag 0EKK grading and Definition Tag 07S1 (definition-free-action); universal stabilizer-algebra calculation supplied by Q20

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-graded-stabilizer-strong-products] to the grading of Step 1 and the ideal equality of Step 2. For each standard basis vector $e_i$ of $M$, obtain a finite expression $1=\sum_j a_{ij}b_{ij}$ with $a_{ij}\in A_{e_i}$ and $b_{ij}\in A_{-e_i}$. Set $B=A_0$. Each $f_{ij}=a_{ij}b_{ij}$ belongs to $B$. These are actual opposite-degree products, rather than arbitrary homogeneous generators; this distinction supplies the homogeneous units in the next step.

source.place: Agent algebraic auxiliary lem-sfb-graded-stabilizer-strong-products to Tag 0EKK; argument preserved in report.md

proof.text: For each $i$, the $f_{ij}$ generate the unit ideal of $B$, so their principal opens cover $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. Taking all finite choices $j_i$ gives a cover by $D(f)$, $f=\prod_i f_{i j_i}$. For $r=0$ the sole product is $f=1$. On $A[1/f]$ each $a_{i j_i}$ is a unit, with inverse $b_{i j_i}\prod_{k\ne i}f_{k j_k}/f$, of degree $-e_i$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Localization at the degree-zero $f$ retains the direct grading: a finite homogeneous sum vanishes iff a power of $f$ kills it, and the original directness then kills each component. In particular the degree-zero ring is $B[1/f]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $D(f)=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$, and its inverse image under $q:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A[1/f]$: the primes in that inverse image are exactly those not containing $f$.

source.place: Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine); algebra.tex Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology); homogeneous-unit calculation supplied

proof.text: Fix one of these $f$ and abbreviate the chosen degree-$e_i$ units by $u_i$. The homomorphism $B[1/f][z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]\to A[1/f]$, $z_i\mapsto u_i$, has inverse sending a homogeneous element $c$ of degree $m$ to $(c u^{-m})z^m$, and extending by finite sums. Indeed $cu^{-m}$ has degree zero; products add degrees, and the two composites fix each homogeneous element and each Laurent monomial. This proves an isomorphism over $B[1/f]$, equivariant because $\rho(u_i)=t_i\otimes u_i$. The spectrum functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] therefore identify $q^{-1}D(f)\to D(f)$ with $T\times_S D(f)\to D(f)$, with translation on the first factor. The tensor identification here is coefficientwise: $R[M]\otimes_R B[1/f]\simeq B[1/f][M]$, $t^m\otimes b\mapsto bt^m$. Thus $q$ has Zariski local sections and each local fibre functor is one free $T$-orbit.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), with explicit homogeneous Laurent inverse; compare Abramovich--Temkin Lemma 5.4.4 (local copy WANTED)

proof.text: The functor $h_Y$ is an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. To verify its quotient property, let $H$ be any fppf sheaf and let $h_X\to H$ be $T$-invariant. On each $D(f)$ pull its section on $X$ back along the identity section of the trivialization in Step 5. On an overlap the two chosen sections differ by a morphism to $T$ (their Laurent coordinates give its unit coordinates), so invariance makes their pullbacks to $H$ equal. Since Zariski open covers are fppf covers [def-pc-fppf-site], they glue uniquely to a section of $H(Y)$. Its pullback to $X$ is the original section: this holds on each trivialization because every point $(t,y)$ is $t$ times the identity section. Uniqueness follows by pulling back to those same local sections. A section of $H(Y)$ gives the natural map $h_Y\to H$ by restriction along each test map to $Y$; conversely evaluate such a map at $\mathrm{id}_Y$. Hence $h_Y$ has precisely the universal property for maps from the orbit presheaf into sheaves. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] it is the required sheafification. Its map from $h_X$ is $q$, induced by $A^T=B\hookrightarrow A$. Since $Y$ is an affine spectrum, this also proves the asserted affineness over $S$.
